cards.title: Used to Form
cards.subtitle: the same form for all persons

examples: We used to play football in this yard.
My dad didn't use to drink coffee.
— Did you use to live here? — Yes, I did.

panels.note: Negatives and questions are built with did, so the main verb goes back to use to.

cards.title: Used to — Be / Get used to — Would — Was going to
cards.subtitle: past habits, getting accustomed, unfulfilled plans

items.case: Used to / Past Simple: past habits or regular past actions that no longer happen
examples: Grandpa used to ride / rode a motorbike when he was young.
I didn't use to like spinach as a child.
items.hint: Used to has one form for all persons; negatives and questions take did.

items.case: Be / Get used to + noun / pronoun / -ing form: be or become accustomed to something
examples: Sailors are used to rough weather. (accustomed, present)
I'm used to waking up at six. (accustomed, present)
She wasn't used to driving on the left. (not accustomed, past)
Ivan is getting used to his new school. (becoming accustomed, present)
After a month abroad he got used to the food. (became accustomed, past)
You'll get used to the noise soon. (will become accustomed, future)

items.case: Would / used to: repeated actions or routines in the past. Would is not used with stative verbs
examples: Every summer we would swim in the river. (also: used to swim)
I used to own a red bicycle. (NOT: would own)

items.case: Was going to: a plan or arrangement in the past that did not happen
examples: I was going to call you, but my phone died.
